Aparajith looks to carve it over the fence and while he does get a good chunk of it, he does not get enough power or elevation to clear the fielder. Simple catch, and Aparajith walks back after a well-compiled 72 and having taken his side to 158!
postText: 8:45pm A thunderous ending to the innings, and that has gotten the Super Gillies closer to where they would have wanted to be. Aparajith was the glue throughout that innings and kept things ticking, even as those around him fell. Tanwar then provided the pyrotechnics alongside his skipper to ensure CSG ransacked 58 in the final five. The Dragons, on the other hand, would feel they could have kept CSG to a much lower score. Aparajith was dropped off the second ball he faced and their fielding in general was not up to scratch. Ashwin and Charavarthy could also not make the most of the conditions, with Bhati and Vignesh the only consistent bright spots in their bowling effort. They will still be confident of chasing this down, but they might have just left the door ajar for the four-time champions. Join us in a bit for the run-chase! Abhishek Tanwar: (On batting lower down and his role) In our team, we have super batters in the top five or six. I have been given that role and I have that freedom (to hit at the death). Low scores do not last for top-quality batters and in the big game, the big players score. This is a par score. The wicket is holding a bit, especially when you bowl it into the wicket. Hopefully, we will come across (as winners).
